# lines.library: Contains

**Status:** Supported (tier `geometry`). In a shipping tier; the lint, type-check, and code-generation gates cover it. No release promises its signature yet.

## Summary

> True when `point` lies on or behind the boundary plane
> (Dot(Normal, point) \<= Distance). Boundary inclusive.

## Signature

```plato
Contains(h: HalfSpace, point: Point3D): Boolean
Contains(h: HalfPlane2D, point: Point2D): Boolean
Contains(s: Slab2D, point: Point2D): Boolean
Contains(s: Slab3D, point: Point3D): Boolean
```

### Law_ContainsCenter

[stdlib/tests/foundation.laws.plato, line 79](../../../../../stdlib/tests/foundation.laws.plato#L79)

```plato
// Same property, stated over AngleInterval's OWN surface.
//
// DOMAIN: AngleInterval reinterprets both Contains and Center as ARC operations
// (intervals.library.plato), so the generic law above does
// not describe this type. Worse, monomorphizing it produces a CHIMERA: the
// interface's linear Center is inlined into the law body (resolution happens
// against IInterval, where the specialization is invisible), while the
// Contains call survives as a call and is re-bound by C# extension-method
// overload resolution to the type's wrap-aware one (tracked as plato-374). Arc
// Contains of a linear midpoint holds for neither reading, and it fails for
// every interval whose stored End - Start exceeds a turn. Restated here on the
// arc surface, where
// the midpoint is Start + Span/2 and containment always holds.
Law_ContainsCenter(self: AngleInterval): Boolean
    => self.Contains(self.Center);
```

### Line 373

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/lines.library.plato, line 373](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/lines.library.plato#L373).

```plato

    // True when `point` lies on or behind the boundary plane
    // (Dot(Normal, point) <= Distance). Boundary inclusive.
    Contains(h: HalfSpace, point: Point3D): Boolean
        => h.Boundary.SignedDistance(point) <= 0.0;
```

### Line 514

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/lines.library.plato, line 514](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/lines.library.plato#L514).

```plato

    //==
    // # Slabs
    //
    // A slab is the preimage of a closed number interval under the linear map
    // p -> Dot(Normal, p), so containment is exactly interval containment.
    // `Contains(IInterval, value)` (P4) is endpoint-inclusive and assumes the
    // interval is stored forward (Start <= End), which is the slab's own invariant.

    // True when the point's signed distance along Normal lies within Interval.
    Contains(s: Slab2D, point: Point2D): Boolean
        => s.Interval.Contains(point.PositionVector.Dot(s.Normal.Vector));
```
